title: Google Launches Gemini 4 Neon at $3 per Million Tokens
dek: Near-flagship reasoning built for coding and agents, faster and cheaper.

facts.label: Lower cost per task than Carbon

caption:
Google just put near-flagship AI on a much cheaper price tag. ⚡

Gemini 4 Neon is the newest member of the Gemini 4 family, sitting between Hydrogen (fast everyday tasks) and Carbon (the hardest long projects). It's priced at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output, with a 1 million-token context window that handles text, images, audio and video. It's live now in the Gemini app, Gemini for business and Google Antigravity.

Google built Neon for coding agents and long tool-heavy sessions. It can even orchestrate parallel Hydrogen subagents. Google says it costs 32% less per task than Carbon at default settings and ranks #1 on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index. Those are Google's own picked benchmarks, so independent testing will tell the real story.

Here at AI Parabellum, we think the bigger signal is the race toward cheaper, smarter agents. Would you switch your coding assistant to Neon? 👇

post_caption:
Carbon-level quality without Carbon-level cost? That's Google's pitch for Gemini 4 Neon.

The new model offers four thinking levels, a 95% discount on cached input and Google's lowest fabrication rate yet in internal tests. A cyber version is also heading to trusted defenders through the Fairwind Program. 🔐
